title: Phased burn concentration and price-kink model
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet models runway and unit economics under a concentrated burn / staged-hire cadence and a non-linear (kinked) pricing response from our enterprise customers. The objective is to show how small changes in per-token price or slab commitments cascade into headcount phasing, dedicated capacity commitments, and runway months. Use for Q1 planning and for the pricing committee discussion Nov 18.

Key assumptions (base):
- Starting cash balance (operating): $120,000,000
- Monthly fixed opex (pre-hiring): $4,200,000
- Average loaded FTE cost (eng/infra/product): $24,000/month (includes payroll tax + benefits + bench overhead)
- GPU reserved capacity commit (monthly): $1,200,000 (can be stepped down with 30d notice with 10% penalty)
- Token revenue mix: 60% hosted API, 25% Dedicated, 15% Private (by $)
- Baseline blended price per 1M tokens: $3.45
- Elasticity breakpoint (kink): -10% price moves have linear elasticity; beyond -10% adoption drops faster (kink) as customers re-architect or switch to E2E caching; we model a concavity parameter.

What this sheet contains:
1) Headcount phasing (quarterly) under three hiring cadence options (stepped, smoothed, burst).
2) Pricing sensitivity grid showing margin and runway under price +/- 30% and under two elasticity regimes (linear, kinked).
3) Capacity commitment decision matrix: when to reduce reserved GPU vs. hire contractors.
4) Recommended mitigation playbook.

1) Headcount phasing (Q4 2026 -> Q3 2027) [simplified table]
Columns: role, Q4-26, Q1-27, Q2-27, Q3-27, notes
Engineering: 78, 84, 92, 100, "ramp backend + serving-runtime hires in Q2 to support dedicated pools"
Product: 12, 14, 16, 17, "console & optimize PMs"
SRE/Infra: 9, 11, 14, 16, "SRE ramp tied to dedicated capacity"
Applied ML / Model Ops: 10, 12, 14, 15, "quantization & model-onboarding team increases Q2"
Sales/CS: 22, 26, 30, 34, "enterprise AE hires Q1->Q2 for Dedicated deals"
Finance/People/Legal: 11, 11, 12, 12, "steady"
Total FTEs: 142, 158, 180, 194

Cost summary from headcount (monthly run-rate at quarter start)
- Payroll run-rate (base): Q4-26 $3.4M; Q1-27 $3.8M; Q2-27 $4.3M; Q3-27 $4.6M
- Incremental contractor/consulting buffer (contingent): plan holds $220k/mo in Q1 then scale to $450k/mo peak (Q2) if we delay hires.

2) Pricing sensitivity grid (select rows)
Grid axes: price change vs. elasticity regime -> outputs: net margin per million tokens, monthly revenue, runway (months to zero cash assuming current spend + hires).
Scenarios (high level snapshots):
- Baseline price (0%): revenue $12.9M/mo; gross margin 48%; runway ~14.3 months (no hires beyond current plan).
- Price -10% (linear elasticity 0.6): revenue $11.1M/mo; gross margin 44%; runway ~12.2 months.
- Price -10% (kinked elasticity 1.2 beyond breakpoint): revenue $10.0M/mo; gross margin 40%; runway ~11.0 months.
- Price -20% (kink): revenue $8.2M/mo; gross margin 34%; runway ~8.0 months.
- Price +15% (demand soft but price stickier): revenue $14.8M/mo; gross margin 52%; runway ~16.5 months.

Interpretation notes:
- The kinked regime amplifies downside: a -10% posted price that triggers re-architecture leads to outsized volume loss compared to linear expectation.
- Runway is highly sensitive to committed GPU spend and the timing of hires: delaying 8 backend hires into Q3 (instead of Q2) recovers ~0.9 months of runway in the -10% kink scenario.

3) Capacity commitment decision matrix (rules-of-thumb)
- If price drops >7% and churn >5% (30d trailing), initiate GPU-Stepdown-Plan A: reduce reserved capacity by 25% with negotiated penalty and activate spot-burst policy for short tail.
- If price drop triggers >10% revenue hit and projected runway <10 months, pause non-critical hires (product features flagged low impact) and move 60% of planned hires to contractors (higher $/month but zero long-term burden).
- Maintain a 3-month runway buffer for Dedicated contract ramp windows (quarterly cadence).

4) Break-even hiring sensitivities (helpful micro-table)
- Each additional backend engineer adds ~0.9% to monthly burn. The expected throughput uplift required to justify the hire (at baseline price) is ~12% increase in hosted API throughput tied to caching improvements.
- Hiring a dedicated SRE (loaded cost $30k/mo) avoids ~$110k/mo in rare outage SLA burn costs if we can reduce incident rate by 25% on a top 10 customer bucket. This is a qualitative trigger we recommend codifying in runbooks.

5) Stress-test slices (short sketches)
A) Rapid price compression (-20%) + delayed enterprise renewals: trigger = CFO triple-check + SR ops all-hands; playbook = block all non-essential hiring, immediate re-negotiate GPU commit, launch "alpha-conserve" feature that gates high-cost routes.
B) Slow price erosion (-5% over 3 months) but higher adoption for low-margin embeddings: playbook = lean hiring, prioritize Optimize (cost toolkit) feature, accelerate quantization program to recover margin.

Open items / questions for pricing committee:
- Should we adopt a formal breakpoint policy (e.g., automatic 20% hiring pause if runway <10 months) or handle on case-by-case?
- Can Sales commit to 60-day accelerated AE ramp funding for strategic Dedicated deals (to offset stepped GPU commitments)?
- What tolerance do we want for moving hires to contractors (max % of engineering headcount on contingent labor)? Current working limit: 15% but could be increased to 25% in an acute downside.

Appendix: quick math snippets
- Runway calculation = cash / (fixed opex + payroll run-rate + GPU reserved) with scenario-modified revenue subtracted.
- Example: Baseline monthly net burn = $4.2M (fixed) + $3.4M (payroll) + $1.2M (GPU) - $12.9M (revenue) = -$4.1M net inflow (positive) => increases runway effectively (but conservative model floors to 0 growth).

Recommendations (top 5):
1) Approve a formal "price-kink" watch with two triggers: (a) published price movement >7% and (b) 30d revenue delta >6%. If both true, convene Pricing + Finance + DevEx within 48h.
2) Move $2.7M of unallocated headcount budget to a contingency pot tied to GPU-stepdown options (gives flexibility to pause hires without impacting pay).
3) Accelerate quantization roadmap items that are low dev-risk and have high immediate cost upside (target $600k/mo margin recovery in 6 months).
4) Pilot a 60-day AE "close fund" to help convert 2 large Dedicated prospects; finance will underwrite up to $400k for accelerated ramp for signings above $1.2M ARR.
5) Codify hiring-to-contractor thresholds in the hiring playbook and validate legal on contractor SLAs and IP.

Notes to reviewer (Sophie):
- This is intentionally compact. I left the full month-by-month workbook as a separate sheet (linked in artifacts) — reviewers should pull the modeling tab for sensitivity graphs.
- Numbers are high level; rounding differences expected vs. the canonical workbook.

Next steps:
- Discussion at Nov 18 Pricing Committee; incorporate feedback and produce a "trigger-runbook" for Dec 1 engineering hiring plan.
- Finance to produce a 13-week cash projection overlay if committee approves price-kink watch.

End of sheet.
